text: EX-99.1 2 crmd_q32026earningspr.htm EX-99.1 Document Exhibit 99.1 CORMEDIX THERAPEUTICS REPORTS THIRD QUARTER 2026 FINANCIAL RESULTS AND PROVIDES BUSINESS UPDATE ‒ Recently announced acquisition of assets of Heron Therapeutics ‒ ‒ Q3 2026 consolidated revenue of $54.5 million ‒ ‒ Q3 2026 net loss of $14.7 million ; Adjusted EBITDA of $3.1 million ‒ ‒ Company maintains FY 2026 revenue and narrows Adjusted EBITDA guidance ‒ ‒ Conference call scheduled for today at 8:30 a.m. Eastern Time ‒ Parsippany, NJ – November 12, 2026 – CorMedix Therapeutics (Nasdaq: CRMD) today announced financial results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026, and provided an update on its business. Recent Corporate Highlights: • CorMedix and Heron Therapeutics, Inc. ("Heron") announced on November 9, 2026, that they have entered into a definitive asset purchase agreement under which CorMedix will acquire substantially all of the assets of Heron. CorMedix believes the transaction will be immediately accretive to earnings and free cash flow upon closing, which it anticipates in the first quarter of 2027, subject to approval by Heron’s stockholders, regulatory clearance and other customary closing conditions. • CorMedix announces $54.5 million of total revenue and grant income ("consolidated revenue") for the third quarter of 2026, above street consensus of $51.2 million, reflecting steady t hird quarter execution in the face of post-TDAPA headwinds for DefenCath. The Company also recognized a net loss of $14.7 million and adjusted EBITDA of $3.1 million (1). Basic and fully diluted earnings per share (EPS) were $(0.19) per share for the quarter. • DefenCath® (taurolidine and heparin) sales contributed $17.2 million of net revenue in the third quarter, driven by largely maintaining utilization of DefenCath by large outpatient dialysis customers in the post-TDAPA period, which impacted price, as well as by a $5.0 million favorable change in estimate related to certain sales allowances. The remaining portfolio contributed total revenue and grant income of $37.3 million . • CorMedix announced on October 19, 2026, that in collaboration with its global development partner Mundipharma, the FDA accepted for review the submission of the sNDA for an expanded indication of REZZAYO for the prophylaxis of invasive fungal disease. The Company anticipates agency action on the application in the first quarter of 2027. • In connection with the Heron asset acquisition, CorMedix entered into a term loan agreement to provide up to $150 million in non-dilutive capital, of which the Company expects to utilize $75 million upon closing. The term loan supports the Company's financial flexibility to invest in our existing operations as well as in new business development opportunities. • The Company maintains full-year 2026 consolidated revenue guidance of $325 to $345 million, narrows full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance to a range of $130 to $140 million from a range of $125 to $140 million, and reduces cash-based OpEx guidance to a range of $140 to $145 million from $145 to $155 million. • In light of recently announced changes to the CMS reimbursement framework, the Company believes it is appropriate to suspend any previously issued 2027 DefenCath revenue guidance and defer future guidance until early 2027. This is the estimated timeframe when the Company expects to have better visibility into 2027 utilization and pricing for customers and any potential upside from Medicare Advantage contracting. • Cash and short-term investments, excluding restricted cash, at September 30, 2026 totaled $355.2 million. Joseph Todisco, Chairman & Chief Executive Officer of CorMedix, commented, “CorMedix will be entering 2027 with two meaningful potential growth drivers. First, our pending acquisition of the Heron assets adds four commercial products used in institutional settings of care and is expected to be immediately accretive to earnings and free cash flow upon closing. With an anticipated revenue contribution of between $125 million and $150 million for the full-year 2027, we expect the Heron transaction to effectively double the Company’s non-DefenCath annual product revenue. Second, the FDA granted Priority Review to the REZZAYO prophylaxis sNDA, with a PDUFA date in the first quarter of 2027. If approved, we plan to commence promotional efforts in the second half of 2027. We continue to execute on our strategy to generate value from DefenCath in the post-TDAPA era as well as deploy our capital in a disciplined manner to drive future growth. With a strong current cash position and access to additional non-dilutive capital from Pharmakon, we believe we are well positioned to integrate Heron, prepare for REZZAYO expanded commercialization, and build a more diversified company." See “Non-GAAP Financial Measures” on the following pages for additional information regarding the use of EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA and a reconciliation to the most comparable GAAP measure. Third Quarter 2026 Financial Highlights For the third quarter of 2026, CorMedix recorded $54.5 million in consolidated revenue, comprised of $17.2 million in sales of DefenCath and $37.3 million associated with the remainder of the portfolio, a decrease from $104.3 million in total revenue in the comparable period of 2025. DefenCath sales decreased year over year largely due to DefenCath's transition to the post-TDAPA period on July 1, 2026, which has resulted in lower net pricing. The decrease in DefenCath sales was partially offset by higher revenue from the acquired Melinta portfolio given there was a full quarter of sales in 2026 compared to one month of sales in 2025 after the acquisition of Melinta closed on August 29, 2025. Total operating expenses in the third quarter of 2026 were $36.6 million, compared with $41.7 million in the third quarter of 2025, a decrease of approximately 12%. The decrease of $5.1 million over the prior period was driven primarily by merger-related and reorganization expenses following the Melinta acquisition in the third quarter of 2025, partially offset by incremental operating expenses from the Melinta acquisition for the full quarter in 2026 relative to only one month of incremental expenses in the prior-year period. Research and development (R&D) expenses in the third quarter of 2026 were $7.0 million, compared with $5.1 million for the same period in 2025. The increase in R&D was primarily due to an increase in personnel and clinical trial services in support of the ongoing clinical programs. Selling and marketing expense increased approximately 4% to $11.7 million in the third quarter of 2026 from $11.2 million in the third quarter of 2025. The increase was primarily due to higher personnel cost associated with the larger product portfolio and related marketing programs. This was partially offset by the cost of the overlapping commercial sales teams for one month of the third quarter of 2025, before synergies were realized in 2026. General and administrative expenses decreased approximately 30% to $17.9 million in the third quarter of 2026 from $25.5 million in the third quarter of 2025. The decrease was primarily attributable to Melinta-related transaction and integration costs incurred in the third quarter of 2025, partially offset by higher costs associated with operating as a combined company following the acquisition, and higher personnel, information technology, legal and facilities costs. CorMedix recorded a net loss of $14.7 million, or $(0.19) per basic and diluted share in the third quarter of 2026, compared with net income of $108.6 million, or $1.42 and $1.26 per basic and diluted share, respectively, in the third quarter of 2025. Net loss in the current period was negatively impacted by $11.5 million of non-cash expense from the remeasurement of contingent consideration associated with the Melinta acquisition. Net income in the third quarter of 2025 was positively impacted by a one-time tax benefit of $59.7 million derived from the realization of deferred tax assets associated with the anticipated use of 100% of CorMedix net operation loss carryforwards. In the third quarter of 2026, CorMedix reported adjusted EBITDA of $3.1 million, compared to adjusted EBITDA of $71.9 million in the third quarter of 2025. Adjusted EBITDA excludes depreciation and amortization, stock-based compensation, interest and other income and expense, changes in contingent consideration, taxes, merger-related costs, and other specified adjustments. The calculation for 2026 also excludes the favorable change in estimate related to sales allowances recorded during the quarter. The Company reported cash and cash equivalents of $355.2 million at September 30, 2026, excluding restricted cash. For the first nine months of 2026, net cash provided by operating activities was $218.3 million, compared with $80.6 million in the first nine months of 2025. The year-over-year increase reflects the higher year-to-date earnings achieved during the current year relative to 2025, as well as working capital movements, including the timing of certain contractual rebate payments. The Company believes that it has sufficient resources to fund operations for at least twelve months from the issuance of the Company’s Quarterly Report on Form 10-Q. Non-GAAP Financial Measures This release includes certain non-GAAP financial measures, including EBITDA and adjusted EBITDA, which are intended as supplemental measures of the Company’s performance that are not required by or presented in accordance with GAAP. Management uses these non-GAAP measures internally to evaluate and manage the Company’s operations and to better understand its business because they facilitate a comparative assessment of the Company’s operating performance relative to its performance based on results calculated under GAAP. These non-GAAP measures also isolate the effects of some items that vary from period to period without any correlation to core operating performance and eliminate certain charges that management believes do not reflect the Company’s operations and underlying operational performance. The Company believes that these non-GAAP measures also provide useful information to investors regarding certain financial and business trends relating to the Company’s financial condition and operating results, which facilitates an evaluation of the financial performance of the Company and its operations on a consistent basis. Providing this information therefore allows investors to make independent assessments of the Company’s financial performance, results of operations and trends while viewing the information through the eyes of management. These non-GAAP measures are subject to limitations. The non-GAAP measures presented in this release may not be comparable to similarly titled measures used by other companies because other companies may not calculate one or more in the same manner. Additionally, the non-GAAP performance measures exclude significant expenses and income that are required by GAAP to be recorded in the Company’s financial statements; do not reflect changes in, or cash requirements for, working capital needs. Further, our historical adjusted results are not intended to project our adjusted results of operations or financial position for any future period. To compensate for these limitations, management presents and considers these non-GAAP measures in conjunction with the Company’s GAAP results; no non-GAAP measure should be considered in isolation from or as alternatives to any measure determined in accordance with GAAP.
